In [[stability theory]], '''hyperstability''' is a property of a system that requires the [[State space representation|state vector]] to remain bounded if the inputs are restricted to belonging to a subset of the set of all possible inputs.<ref name=ANDERSON>Brian D. O Anderson, "A Simplified Viewpoint of Hyperstability", ''IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, June 1968''<!-- Available at https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel5/81/27851/01242848.pdf?arnumber=1242848 also --></ref> 

Definition:<ref name=ZINOBER>Zinober, Deterministic control of uncertain systems, 1990<!-- Available at https://books.google.com/books?id=OKGmg4uml84C--></ref> A system is hyperstable if there are two constants <math>k_1 \ge 0, k_2 \ge 0</math> such that any state trajectory of the system satisfies the inequality:

:<math>\| x(t) \| < k_1 \|x(0)\| + k_2, \, \forall t \ge 0 </math>
